**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of hyperparathyroidism is established for any individual, and for this edge the ascertainment problem is decisive: the largest anchor confirmed hyperparathyroidism in only FOUR patients while measuring parathyroid hormone in only 2.8 percent of the population, so its case count cannot support a rate and a four-case numerator in a 580-patient cohort is compatible with a wide range of true prevalence; two of the three anchors measure serum calcium rather than parathyroid hormone, and the catalog carries no hypercalcaemia identity, so the parathyroid diagnosis is inferred from a calcium proxy; the control group in the one anchor with a comparator comprises only 15 patients, which cannot support a precise between-group estimate even though the direction is clear; and no anchor separates lithium-induced parathyroid hyperplasia from an incidental or pre-existing adenoma, which the same anchor cannot exclude because it did not image the glands; individual claims require a dated lithium start, stop, dose and serum-level timeline with serial corrected calcium and parathyroid hormone measured before and after initiation, neck imaging where a gland lesion is suspected, and exclusion of primary hyperparathyroidism predating lithium therapy, malignancy-associated and familial hyperparathyroidism, thiazide diuretics, and vitamin D deficiency.

### `bipolar-disorder` → `tardive-dyskinesia` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Antipsychotic medication prescribed during treatment of an affective disorder is associated with tardive dyskinesia at quantified rates in the located antipsychotic-exposure literature, and NO LOCATED ANCHOR IS A BIPOLAR COHORT, so the edge is registered at association only with that population limit stated on its face: the 2017 systematic review and meta-analysis of 41 studies and 11,493 patients in the period of second-generation antipsychotic use (mean age 42.8 years, 66.4 percent male, 77.1 percent schizophrenia-spectrum disorders) reports a global mean tardive dyskinesia prevalence of 25.3 percent (95 percent CI 22.7-28.1), lower in current second-generation antipsychotic arms (20.7 percent, 95 percent CI 16.6-25.4, N = 5,103) than in current first-generation arms (30.0 percent, 95 percent CI 26.4-33.8, N = 5,062; Q = 9.17, p = 0.002), and particularly low in first-generation-naive treatment arms (7.2 percent, four studies) against cohorts with likely prior first-generation exposure (23.4 percent, 28 studies, p < 0.001), so the located gradient runs with antipsychotic generation and prior exposure rather than with any psychiatric diagnosis (PMID 28146614); and the 2026 secondary analysis of the IRL-GRey late-life depression trial cohort reports incident tardive dyskinesia in 16 of 255 participants without baseline dyskinesia (6.3 percent) by the end of the venlafaxine lead-in phase, all of them non-remitters, rising to 21 of 117 randomized non-remitters (17.9 percent) by the end of the randomised aripiprazole-or-placebo augmentation phase, with tardive dyskinesia defined as an Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale item 8 score of at least 1 (PMID 42030922). The registered claim is the narrowest the two anchors jointly permit: that antipsychotic exposure during treatment of an affective disorder is associated with incident tardive dyskinesia at the rates the anchors report, with the exposure being the prescribed medication rather than the psychiatric condition, with the meta-analytic gradient attributable to agent generation and exposure history rather than to diagnosis, and with NO bipolar-specific incidence available anywhere in the located evidence.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of tardive dyskinesia is established for any individual: the exposure in both anchors is prescribed antipsychotic medication rather than the bipolar disorder itself, and NO ANCHOR IS A BIPOLAR COHORT, the closest mood-population anchor being a late-life DEPRESSION cohort while the meta-analysis population is 77.1 percent schizophrenia-spectrum, so every rate on this edge is a treatment-class rate carried across diagnoses rather than a bipolar rate; the incident anchor's case definition is an Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale item 8 score of at least 1, which its own authors describe as highly sensitive but non-specific, its incident case counts are small (16 of 255 and 21 of 117), its sex-stratified cognitive findings are exploratory without correction for multiple comparisons, and the two incident figures are measured at different phase endpoints in different denominators (the full cohort against the non-remitters entering randomisation) with NO arm-specific aripiprazole-versus-placebo incidence reported, so no agent-specific attributable risk may be derived from it; the meta-analysis measures prevalence rather than incidence and reports that tardive dyskinesia severity was too poorly reported across its studies for meta-analysis, so the clinical burden of its identified cases is unquantified; and no anchor includes an antipsychotic-free bipolar control arm, so bipolar disorder's own contribution to abnormal movement is not separable from the medication within these designs. Individual claims require a dated antipsychotic start, stop, dose, formulation and route timeline with dated Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale examinations before and after initiation, a documented antipsychotic-free interval where one exists, and exclusion of spontaneous orofacial dyskinesia, of other dopamine-blocking agents including metoclopramide and prochlorperazine, of withdrawal-emergent dyskinesia after dose reduction or cessation, and of Huntington disease, Wilson disease, stroke and other structural or degenerative movement disorders.

### `rumination-syndrome` → `bulimia-nervosa` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Rumination syndrome and bulimia nervosa co-occur at a rate far above matched controls, and the single largest comparative study designs the finding as a case-control contrast rather than a coincidence of presentation: a tertiary-centre case-control study of 24 adults with rumination syndrome against 48 age- and gender-matched controls reports a history of eating disorder in 37.5 percent of rumination syndrome patients against 4.2 percent of controls (Fisher exact p=0.0002), with anorexia nervosa at 16.7 percent against 0 percent (p=0.005) and bulimia nervosa at 21.1 percent against 0 percent (p=0.001), and with eating-disorder history surviving multivariable adjustment as an independent predictor of rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 16.4 (p=0.0033) (PMID 33988353); an adolescent case series of eight referred girls reports six diagnosed with rumination syndrome, most of whom carried a co-occurring anxiety, depressive, or eating-disorder diagnosis including anorexia and bulimia (PMID 42217214); and a bidirectional 101-patient paediatric cohort separating early-childhood-onset from adolescent-onset rumination syndrome reports the adolescent-onset phenotype as the one carrying the eating-disorder and mood comorbidity, with 23 percent depression and 40 percent anxiety confined to the adolescent-onset group against 0 percent and 14 percent in the early-onset group, and with the authors concluding explicitly that the pathogenesis and natural history of the two onset strata may be distinct (PMID 38504395); recorded as documented association only, and with the direction of the relationship carried as unresolved because the largest anchor's own model treats eating-disorder history as a RISK FACTOR FOR rumination syndrome rather than the reverse, so the edge is registered as a bidirectional co-occurrence requiring separate documentation of each diagnosis rather than as a claim that either produces the other.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation is established in either direction, and the located anchor argues actively against fixing a direction: the largest comparative study modelled prior eating-disorder history as a risk factor for rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 16.4 rather than modelling rumination syndrome as a risk factor for a later eating-disorder diagnosis, so the temporal ordering is asserted by that design rather than demonstrated by it; a substantial share of the apparent overlap is plausibly diagnostic rather than causal, because rumination syndrome is classified within the feeding and eating disorders in current diagnostic nomenclature and a prior eating-disorder label may reflect reclassification of the same undifferentiated regurgitation behaviour rather than a distinct illness preceding it; the two entities also differ in mechanism, since rumination syndrome is an effortless postprandial retrograde flow of undigested contents driven by an automatic autonomic reflex, whereas bulimia nervosa is a deliberate binge-and-purge behaviour, so shared abdominal distress, dietary restriction, and body-image disturbance can produce convergent presentations without either driving the other; and the adolescent anchors are a case series and a single-centre bidirectional cohort, neither of which includes a rumination-syndrome-free comparison group for the eating-disorder outcome. Individual claims require a dated, separately signed diagnosis of bulimia nervosa with documented binge and purge episodes, a dated rumination-syndrome diagnosis documenting effortless regurgitation of undigested food, the chronology of which diagnosis came first, and explicit clinician exclusion of vomiting as a learned behaviour or of regurgitation as a learned behaviour before the two are recorded as co-occurring.

### `rumination-syndrome` → `anxiety-disorder` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Anxiety is the most consistently reported psychiatric correlate of rumination syndrome across three independent designs that span adult, adolescent, and paediatric populations, and the largest of them reports the association surviving multivariable adjustment: a tertiary-centre case-control study of 24 adults with rumination syndrome against 48 matched controls reports 83.3 percent of rumination syndrome patients carrying a psychiatric disorder against 50.0 percent of controls (p=0.0062), with anxiety present in 37.5 percent and depression in 29.2 percent, and with psychiatric-disorder history remaining an independent adjusted predictor of rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 4.47 (p=0.029) (PMID 33988353); an adolescent case series reports that most of the six adolescents diagnosed with rumination syndrome carried co-occurring emotional or psychiatric difficulty, explicitly naming anxiety alongside depression and eating disorders, and identifies delayed diagnosis resulting from the presentation being mistaken for reflux or vomiting (PMID 42217214); and a bidirectional 101-patient paediatric cohort reports anxiety in 40 percent of adolescent-onset disease against 14 percent of early-childhood-onset disease (p=0.004), the same stratum that carries 23 percent depression and the one the authors identify as potentially distinct in pathogenesis (PMID 38504395); recorded as documented association only, with the same reversed modelling direction carried openly, since the largest anchor again treats psychiatric history as a risk factor for rumination syndrome rather than the converse.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of anxiety is established for any individual, and the direction is unresolved for the same reasons that apply to the file's eating-disorder edge: the largest comparative anchor modelled psychiatric-disorder history as a risk factor FOR rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 4.47, not rumination syndrome as a risk factor for a subsequent anxiety diagnosis, so the temporal ordering is a design choice rather than a finding; a substantial component of the overlap is plausibly reactive rather than causal, because a chronic, visible, embarrassing, and socially stigmatising regurgitation behaviour with associated weight loss and meal avoidance is an obvious precipitant of anxiety and of social avoidance, and the located series documents embarrassment and distress as central features without establishing whether any anxiety preceded them; the two conditions also share a documented transdiagnostic mechanism in which repetitive negative thinking and emotion-regulation difficulty appear in both, which permits either condition to recruit the other; and no located anchor measures anxiety before the onset of regurgitation. Individual claims require a dated anxiety diagnosis with documented symptom history predating or postdating regurgitation onset, a dated rumination-syndrome diagnosis, and clinician separation of situational anxiety about the illness from a pre-existing anxiety disorder.

### `salivary-gland-cancer` → `dysphagia` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Dysphagia is the best-quantified symptomatic burden in the located malignant parotid cohort and is documented as a presenting symptom across independent salivary-gland carcinoma sites: a survivorship-clinic retrospective study of 62 surgically treated malignant parotid tumour patients reports clinically relevant dysphagia symptoms on the Eating Assessment Tool in 32.3 percent at last follow-up, with patients treated with surgery plus adjuvant chemoradiation having significantly worse swallowing scores than those treated with surgery alone (p=0.03) and patients treated with surgery plus adjuvant radiotherapy having significantly worse physical and social-emotional quality of life than surgery alone (p<0.01 and p=0.01 respectively) (PMID 38837232); a PRISMA systematic review of 44 articles covering 195 patients with oropharyngeal adenoid cystic carcinoma reports presenting symptoms to be mainly pain or discomfort (n=31) followed by a palpable mass (n=19) and dysphagia (n=12), with the base of tongue the most common subsite at 73 percent, positive cervical nodes in 22.3 percent at diagnosis, and distant metastases in 36 percent of those who progressed, primarily to the lungs (n=26) (PMID 42371638); and a dedicated analysis of 29 cases of malignant salivary gland tumours of the tongue confirms that tongue subsite is a recognised and separately reported presentation category (PMID 41793734); recorded as documented association only, with the treatment gradient carried as an explicit confounder rather than as evidence of tumour-driven dysphagia alone.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of dysphagia is established for any individual, and the located cohort is explicit that treatment is a co-driver: the 32.3 percent dysphagia figure is a survivorship-clinic prevalence at last follow-up in patients who had already undergone surgery, and the same cohort reports that the dysphagia difference is significant between surgery plus chemoradiation and surgery alone, which means the measured burden is at least partly iatrogenic and cannot be attributed to the tumour; base-of-tongue and oral-cavity subsites are mechanically obstructive by anatomy rather than by disease mechanism, so a mass at that subsite produces dysphagia through physical obstruction of the swallowing lumen and a base-of-tongue adenoid cystic carcinoma is a different clinical entity from a parotid malignancy even though both are salivary gland carcinoma; the systematic review is a synthesis of 44 small studies with 195 total patients and no pooled estimate, so its counts describe a literature rather than a population; and none of the three anchors separates dysphagia caused by the primary tumour from dysphagia caused by surgery, radiation-induced fibrosis, neck dissection, xerostomia-induced dentition change, or a distant metastasis, all of which are plausible in this population. Individual claims require a dated dysphagia assessment with an instrumental or validated clinical measure, documented tumour subsite and stage, a dated treatment timeline separating pre-treatment from post-treatment swallowing status, and exclusion of post-surgical stricture, radiation fibrosis, and metastatic obstruction.

### `salivary-gland-cancer` → `depressive-disorder` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Depressive symptoms are measured directly in the located malignant parotid survivorship cohort and are reported to worsen with adjuvant treatment, which makes this the one emotional-burden edge in this file supported by an instrument rather than inferred: the same 62-patient cohort reports elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-8 in 15.5 percent at last follow-up, alongside social-emotional quality of life significantly worse in patients who received adjuvant radiotherapy (p=0.01) and adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (p=0.02) than in patients treated with surgery alone, and anxiety on the GAD-7 in 7.1 percent and insomnia in 7.2 percent (PMID 38837232); the oropharyngeal adenoid cystic carcinoma systematic review supplies the disease-trajectory context, documenting disease progression in 86 of 195 patients over the reviewed follow-up with distant metastases in 36 percent of those who progressed, which is the morbidity trajectory against which a mood consequence would be expected to accrue (PMID 42371638); and the SWOG S1609 DART phase II basket trial salivary gland tumour cohort supplies the contemporary interventional-design reference point against which the observational mood signal is bounded (PMID 42499790); recorded as documented association only, with the 15.5 percent figure carried as a symptom-screen prevalence rather than a depression diagnosis rate.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of a depressive disorder is established for any individual, and the instrument used is the central limitation: PHQ-8 is a screening instrument, and the located cohort reports the prevalence of ELEVATED SYMPTOMS rather than of diagnosed major depressive disorder, so the 15.5 percent figure cannot be read as a depression diagnosis rate and no anchor in this edge reports a structured diagnostic interview; the reported association is explicitly entangled with treatment, since the cohort finds mood and quality-of-life outcomes worse in patients who received adjuvant therapy, which means the mood burden may be treatment-induced, disease-induced, or both, and the design cannot apportion between them; the cohort is a survivorship population drawn from a single multidisciplinary clinic with 62 patients, which is a selected group; the systematic review reports progression and metastasis but reports no mood outcomes at all, so it contributes disease-severity context only and cannot be cited as mood evidence; and mood comorbidity after a head and neck malignancy is an expected finding in any cancer survivorship population, so the signal is not specific to salivary gland carcinoma and cannot distinguish a salivary-gland-specific route from a generic cancer-survivorship route. Individual claims require a structured diagnostic interview establishing a depressive disorder as distinct from adjustment disorder, grief, or a PHQ-8 screen alone, with dated onset relative to both diagnosis and treatment.

### `salivary-gland-cancer` → `xerostomia` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Salivary gland carcinoma produces dry mouth through two independent routes, the disease route and the treatment route, and the located evidence documents the treatment route in depth: a mechanistic review of radiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction establishes that ionizing radiation damages salivary glands because of their proximity to common head and neck tumour sites, that damage results in loss of secretory function causing severe and chronic reductions in salivary flow, and that this leads directly to the patient-reported sensation of dry mouth termed xerostomia, with the described chronic mechanisms including decreased acinar differentiation markers, increased acinar cell proliferation, immune and inflammatory dysregulation, metabolic changes including increases in amino acids and reductions in glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation, fibrosis, and dysregulated neuronal responses (PMID 38808518); a rapid evidence review of salivary gland disorders supplies the general clinical framing for salivary gland disease and its functional consequences (PMID 38905553); and the malignant parotid survivorship cohort establishes that this is a survivorship-relevant burden measured in a treated salivary gland malignancy population rather than a theoretical concern (PMID 38837232); recorded as documented association only, with the disease route carried as a separate hypothesized vector that no located anchor measures.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of xerostomia is established for any individual, and the two routes cannot be separated by the located evidence: the mechanistic review describes radiation damage in head and neck cancer populations generally and does not isolate salivary gland carcinoma as a subsite, so applying it to a salivary gland primary requires an inference the source does not make; that review also identifies the absence of a standard of care for permanent restoration of salivary function and describes the mechanisms as elusive, which is a statement about mechanism rather than about the robustness of the radiation-to-xerostomia association, which is nonetheless the more firmly established of the two routes; the rapid evidence review covers salivary gland disorders broadly and is not specific to malignancy; the survivorship cohort is registered for population relevance but the located abstract does not report a xerostomia instrument or prevalence, so it cannot serve as the quantitative anchor for this edge; and the disease route, in which a parotid or submandibular tumour replaces functioning gland tissue and a resection removes it, is documented in none of the three anchors and is carried here as a hypothesized second vector only. Individual claims require a dated salivary flow measurement or a validated xerostomia instrument, documented gland involvement and subsite, a dated radiotherapy timeline with dose and field coverage of the remaining salivary tissue, and separation of pre-treatment from post-treatment dryness.

### `samter-s-triad` → `chronic-sinusitis` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** The one edge in this file that can be stated without qualification is chronic rhinosinusitis, because it is a definitional component of the syndrome rather than a consequence inferred from it, and the located evidence describes the phenotype precisely enough to make the co-occurrence specific: a 2024 mechanistic and management review of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug-exacerbated respiratory disease characterises the syndrome by the simultaneous presence of asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug and aspirin intolerance, and states that despite maximal and comprehensive medical treatment the disease tends to be severe, with difficult-to-treat asthma and highly aggressive and recurrent ethmoidal polyposis (PMID 39665076); a 2023 unified-airway review of aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease characterises the condition by abnormal arachidonic acid metabolism leading to chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, asthma, and upper and lower respiratory symptoms following ingestion of cyclooxygenase-1-inhibiting nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and reports that conventional medical management for both asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis is often inadequate, with endoscopic sinus surgery followed by continued medical management and optional aspirin desensitization frequently improving symptoms and objective disease measures (PMID 36283868); and the 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline on Adult Sinusitis supplies the current diagnostic and management standard against which the syndrome's sinus component is evaluated (PMID 40741969); recorded as documented co-occurrence requiring separate documentation, expressly NOT as a claim that the syndrome causes its own defining component.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** No causal claim is made or available here, and the edge's own causation status says so directly: chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis is one of the three criteria that define this syndrome, so an assertion that the syndrome produces the sinusitis is circular and is expressly disclaimed rather than argued. What the edge records is a co-occurrence with a distinct operational consequence, namely that a veteran whose record carries only the label Samter's triad has not thereby had chronic rhinosinusitis independently documented, characterised by extent, side, and severity, or linked to a treatment plan, and the located evidence shows this matters because the sinus disease is described as highly aggressive, recurrent, and frequently requiring repeat endoscopic sinus surgery. The treatment gradient is also carried openly: the located reviews attribute symptom improvement to surgery plus desensitization, which means the functional burden attributed to the syndrome is partly treatment-dependent and cannot be assigned to disease alone. Individual claims require a dated otolaryngology assessment with endoscopy or imaging documenting chronic rhinosinusitis independently of the triad label, documented extent and polyp burden, and a treatment timeline.

### `samter-s-triad` → `asthma` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Asthma is the second definitional component of this syndrome, and the located evidence describes its severity and the consequences of treating it jointly with the sinus component: the 2024 mechanistic and management review characterises the syndrome as the simultaneous presence of asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug and aspirin intolerance, and states that despite maximal and comprehensive medical treatment the disease tends to be severe, with difficult-to-treat asthma specifically named as a feature (PMID 39665076); the 2023 unified-airway review states that diagnosis is clinical and may involve an aspirin challenge, that inflammatory biomarkers may be useful for diagnosis and treatment monitoring, and that conventional medical management for asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis is often inadequate, with endoscopic sinus surgery followed by continued medical management and or without aspirin desensitization frequently improving symptoms and objective disease measures (PMID 36283868); and a 2026 surgical-outcome cohort of 70 patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps and comorbid asthma undergoing revision endoscopic sinus surgery provides quantified evidence that the asthma and sinus disease behave as one treatment unit, showing that patients with a preoperative Completeness of Surgery Index below 70 had significantly greater improvement on both the sino-nasal outcome test and the Asthma Control Test, with the asthma-control improvement reaching 3.9 versus 0.88 in uncontrolled asthma (p=0.029) (PMID 41045292); recorded as documented co-occurrence requiring separate documentation, expressly NOT as a claim that the syndrome causes its own defining component.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** No causal claim is made or available here, and the causation status disclaims the circular reading explicitly: asthma is one of the three criteria defining this syndrome, so asserting that the syndrome produces the asthma is circular. The located surgery cohort is the only anchor that reports a quantitative asthma outcome, and it is registered as evidence that the two components respond to a shared intervention rather than as evidence of causation between them, because what it demonstrates is that incomplete sinus surgery predicts worse asthma control after revision, which is a statement about coupled treatment response and not about one condition producing the other. The severity characterisation in the review anchors is qualitative and unreferenced in the located abstracts, so its magnitude cannot be quantified from these sources, and no located anchor reports a prevalence of severe or difficult-to-treat asthma within diagnosed syndrome cohorts, because by definition all of them have asthma. Individual claims require a dated pulmonology assessment documenting asthma severity, control, and current therapy independently of the triad label, plus documentation of whether an aspirin challenge was performed and with what result.

### `scleredema` → `diabetes-mellitus` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** The diabetes association in scleredema is the largest and best-replicated of its three classical associates, and the located evidence includes both a multicentre series and a prospective screening study in a diabetes population: a multicentre retrospective study of 44 patients with scleredema reports that the most common associated disorders were endocrine and metabolic diseases, with 30 of the 44 patients suffering from diabetes, mostly type 2, concludes that scleredema is a chronic debilitating disease associated with diabetes and metabolic syndrome, and recommends that treatment of the primary disease including strict glycaemic control combined with physical therapy be employed (PMID 26304054); a prospective screening study of 113 consecutive patients with diabetes identified 11 new scleroedema adultorum of Buschke patients, a 9.7 percent prevalence, ALL of whom had type 2 diabetes, and characterised the newly identified cases with a focus on lipid metabolism abnormalities and vascular complications (PMID 33952255); and a case report of scleredema diabeticorum in a patient with poorly controlled diabetes documents extensive trunk involvement in a cuirasse pattern with associated restrictive lung disease, cutaneous ultrasonographic dermal thickening, and the observation that cutaneous hardness secondary to scleredema may cause limited mobility with respiratory manifestations assessable mainly where extensive scleredema involves trunk and shoulders (PMID 33865279); recorded as documented association only, with the direction carried as unresolved and the classic post-infectious teaching explicitly nulled.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of diabetes mellitus is established for any individual, and in this edge the direction is genuinely bidirectional and unresolvable from the located evidence: the multicentre series reports diabetes as a comorbidity OF scleredema in 30 of 44 patients, while the screening study reports scleredema as a newly identified condition IN a diabetes population, and neither design establishes which came first, so the honest reading is co-occurrence enriched in both directions rather than a route. The shared driver is plausibly upstream of both, since both conditions are associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and hyperinsulinaemia, and the screening study's own focus on dyslipidaemia and vascular complications indicates that the metabolic phenotype surrounds both diagnoses; the classic teaching that scleredema follows streptococcal or other infection is directly CONTRADICTED by the largest located series, which explicitly reports that a preceding respiratory tract infection was NOT a feature in its 44 patients, and that null is carried openly in the evidence gaps rather than omitted, because it changes what a reviewer should look for; the 9.7 percent screening prevalence is from a single tertiary centre in consecutively screened diabetes patients and may not generalise; and the case report is a single patient. Individual claims require a dated type 2 diabetes diagnosis with glycaemic control data and a dated scleredema diagnosis with distribution documented, plus exclusion of monoclonal gammopathy and of preceding streptococcal infection as alternative associates.

### `scleredema` → `multiple-myeloma` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** The plasma-cell dyscrasia association is the most clinically consequential of the three classical scleredema associates, because it is the one in which the skin disease can be the presenting sign of an underlying malignancy, and the located evidence establishes this across a multicentre series, a treatment-response case report, and a documented progression case: a multicentre retrospective study of 44 patients with scleredema reports monoclonal gammopathies confirmed in 5 cases and that systemic corticosteroids and immunosuppressive drugs were reserved for patients with severe disease in whom phototherapy had failed or FOR PATIENTS WITH MULTIPLE MYELOMA, with 2 of the 44 patients dying of cardiovascular complications due to myeloma and severe diabetes (PMID 26304054); a case report of monoclonal gammopathy-associated scleredema adultorum of Buschke in a patient with diabetes mellitus treated successfully with intravenous immunoglobulin and narrow-band ultraviolet B phototherapy documents the dyscrasia-skin pairing as a treatable entity (PMID 34858014); and a case report of scleredema in the setting of monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance with progression to multiple myeloma documents the dyscrasia evolving to frank myeloma with new-onset Raynaud phenomenon, splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and the development of a plasmacytoma (PMID 37701163); recorded as documented association only, with the explicit clinical reading that the skin disease signals a plasma-cell disorder requiring screening rather than causing one.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of multiple myeloma is established for any individual, and the located evidence actually runs against a causal reading of the skin-to-marrow direction: the multicentre series reports monoclonal gammopathy as a comorbidity identified in patients already carrying the skin diagnosis, with the myeloma deaths recorded as deaths FROM a malignancy these patients independently had, and the progression case documents the haematological course moving from monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance to myeloma with the skin disease as a co-traveler rather than as an agent, so the honest reading is that scleredema is a marker that can accompany or precede a plasma-cell dyscrasia. The alternative and partly competing reading is real and is carried openly: monoclonal immunoglobulin itself is proposed in the located literature as contributing to dermal mucin deposition, which would make the paraprotein a contributor rather than a bystander, and the located case report of paraproteinemia-associated scleredema responding to thalidomide is consistent with a paraprotein-mediated mechanism, but no located anchor in this edge tests that mechanism and it is recorded as an alternative rather than adopted. The 5-of-44 figure carries no confidence interval, and no located anchor reports a myeloma-free comparison group for the scleredema outcome. Individual claims require serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation, serum free light chains, and a documented bone marrow assessment, since the entire screening proposition is unimplementable without them.

### `scleredema` → `interstitial-lung-disease` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Extensive scleredema is reported to carry a restrictive pulmonary consequence, and the located evidence documents both the functional pattern and the proposed route: a case report of scleredema diabeticorum in a patient with poorly controlled diabetes describes extensive scleredema adultorum of the trunk in a cuirasse pattern associated with restrictive lung disease, with cutaneous ultrasonography revealing marked thickening of the dermis and multiple echogenic spots, and states explicitly that cutaneous hardness secondary to scleredema may cause limited mobility, that respiratory manifestations may therefore be associated and assessed mainly in cases of extensive scleredema involving trunk and shoulders, and that cutaneous ultrasonography may be useful to monitor disease evolution and confirm the diagnosis (PMID 33865279); the multicentre series of 44 patients reports that phototherapy was the treatment associated with higher although partial response, that systemic corticosteroids and immunosuppressive drugs were reserved for severe disease, and that two patients died of cardiovascular complications due to myeloma and severe diabetes, describing scleredema as a chronic debilitating disease (PMID 26304054); and a separate scleroderma-mimic case describes a patient with diffuse skin thickening of face, neck, arms, forearms, thighs, chest, and back, sparing the hands and feet, with associated arthralgia, dysphagia, and dyspnoea on exertion, a restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing, and interstitial lung fibrosis on high-resolution computed tomography, diagnosed on biopsy as scleredema rather than systemic sclerosis (PMID 30088450); recorded as documented association only, with the route named as hypothesized and the entity-identity problem carried openly.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of an interstitial lung disease is established for any individual, and the strongest located support is a single case: the route described is a chest-wall and shoulder-girdle mechanical restriction from cutaneous hardness limiting chest-wall excursion, NOT an intrinsic parenchymal lung disease, and the located abstract for that case explicitly frames the respiratory manifestations as mechanical and as assessable mainly where extensive disease involves the trunk and shoulders. That distinction is material, because the catalog's interstitial-lung-disease identity denotes a parenchymal process with its own established routes, and a restrictive pattern produced by chest-wall induration is a different entity with a different treatment and a different evidentiary standard. The third anchor is more troubling for this edge: its patient had interstitial lung fibrosis on high-resolution computed tomography AND a restrictive pulmonary pattern, but that patient was diagnosed with scleredema as a scleroderma mimic and had MYELOMA, so the fibrosis in that case may be attributable to the underlying plasma-cell dyscrasia, to the excluded systemic sclerosis differential, or to scleredema, and the located abstract cannot apportion. Individual claims require pulmonary function testing with diffusion capacity, high-resolution computed tomography, exclusion of an underlying plasma-cell dyscrasia, and a documented distinction between chest-wall mechanical restriction and intrinsic parenchymal disease.

### `scleritis` → `uveitis` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Concomitant uveitis is the best-documented ocular companion of scleritis, and the largest located registry quantifies it both as a marker of more severe disease and as the single strongest predictor of structural complications: the AutoInflammatory Disease Alliance Network scleritis registry reports 154 patients with 218 eyes of non-infectious scleritis, records 102 ocular complications in 58 patients across 87 eyes, finds the most frequent complications to be cataract, scleral and corneal thinning, and glaucoma or increased ocular pressure, and reports that ocular complications were significantly more frequent among patients with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (p<0.0001) and with CONCOMITANT UVEITIS (p=0.023) (PMID 42105127); a population-based United Kingdom analysis of 10,939,823 patients with 2,946 incident scleritis cases characterises scleritis as a disease defined by its associations with infectious and immune-mediated inflammatory disease (PMID 33728815); and a single-centre cohort of 69 patients with 96 eyes reports non-infectious scleritis in 56 eyes (58.3 percent) against 40 eyes (41.7 percent) presumed infectious, with idiopathic disease and spondyloarthropathy common in the non-infectious group and tuberculosis-associated disease predominating in the presumed infectious group, and with the authors stressing the need for careful etiologic evaluation in tuberculosis-endemic settings (PMID 42377600); recorded as documented association only, with the registry's own definitional reservation carried openly rather than argued around.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the largest anchor explicitly declines to treat the relationship as a complication at all: the scleritis registry states that uveitis and peripheral ulcerative keratitis were considered EXTENSIONS OF THE INFLAMMATORY PROCESS rather than true structural complications, which is a definitional choice that this edge adopts rather than disputes, meaning the located evidence treats uveitis as a concurrent expression of the same disease rather than a consequence of scleritis. The reported association is therefore not a temporal sequence, and the p=0.023 figure describes how often complications occur in eyes that already carry concomitant uveitis, not what fraction of uveitis follows scleritis. The population-based anchor supplies the association structure but its located abstract does not report uveitis-specific incidence, and the Indonesian cohort is explicitly limited by its retrospective design, incomplete follow-up, and limited microbiological confirmation, with a high proportion of tuberculosis-associated cases that constrains generalisation. Individual claims require a dated ophthalmology assessment documenting uveitis independently, with slit-lamp or anterior-segment OCT evidence and an infectious workup separating non-infectious from tuberculosis-associated or other presumed infectious disease, since the located cohort shows the infectious proportion is not negligible even in a non-endemic-pattern clinic.

**Reviewer questions specific to this edge:**

### `scleritis` → `rheumatoid-arthritis` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Rheumatoid arthritis is the systemic disease most consistently associated with scleritis, and the located evidence spans a population-based analysis of 10,939,823 patients, an EMR-wide review designed specifically to avoid referral bias, and a dedicated review of the rheumatoid ocular manifestations: the population-based United Kingdom analysis of 2,946 incident scleritis cases against 12,020 matched controls characterises scleritis as a disease whose defining epidemiology is its association with immune-mediated inflammatory disease, with adjustment for age, sex, deprivation index, race or ethnicity, smoking status, nation, and body mass index (PMID 33728815); a health-system-wide electronic-record analysis of all charts carrying systemic autoimmune and scleritis diagnoses states explicitly that prior series assessed the relationship between systemic autoimmune disorders and scleritis only in patients referred for rheumatology or ocular inflammation, which introduces referral bias, and that the EMR-wide review was conducted to determine the prevalence of both and which disorders carried the highest relative risk of developing scleritis (PMID 33407267); and a review of rheumatoid arthritis-associated ocular disease reports that scleritis and peripheral ulcerative keratitis are less common than dry eye disease but represent severe inflammatory complications generally requiring systemic immunosuppression, with escalation to biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs including tumour necrosis factor inhibitors and rituximab supported for refractory scleritis and corneal melt, though the evidence is described as largely observational (PMID 42122940); recorded as documented association only with the direction of the relationship stated explicitly.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of rheumatoid arthritis is established for any individual, and the direction here is the reverse of the clinical sequence: in every located design the systemic disease is the antecedent and the ocular manifestation is the consequent, so the clinically operative arrow runs rheumatoid-arthritis to scleritis, and this edge is registered as the reciprocal view of that relationship rather than as a claim that scleritis produces rheumatoid arthritis. The located evidence does not permit even a clean reciprocal reading, because the health-system review reports only prevalence of co-diagnosis and relative risk of developing scleritis from the systemic side, and its own stated motivation is that prior work was referral-biased, which means the magnitude of any association is better estimated from the population anchor than from the ophthalmology-clinic literature. The dedicated rheumatoid-ocular review is a narrative synthesis rather than a pooled estimate, and it states plainly that the biologic-escalation evidence is largely observational. Individual claims require a dated rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis with serology, rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide status, disease activity measures, and a dated scleritis diagnosis, and the reviewing clinician should note that the temporal sequence runs from the systemic disease to the eye, not the reverse.

### `scleritis` → `systemic-lupus-erythematosus` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Systemic lupus erythematosus is the second major systemic disease associated with scleritis, and the located evidence supplies the population-level association structure, the referral-bias correction, and a directly documented ocular manifestation: the population-based United Kingdom analysis of 2,946 incident scleritis cases against 12,020 matched controls estimates the associations of scleritis with immune-mediated inflammatory disease with multivariable adjustment for age, sex, deprivation, race or ethnicity, smoking, nation, and body mass index (PMID 33728815); the health-system-wide electronic-record review states that prior series assessed systemic autoimmune disorders in scleritis only in referred patients and corrects for that referral bias across all charts carrying both diagnoses (PMID 33407267); and a secondary cohort analysis of a population-based lupus cohort examines the risks of ophthalmic disorders in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, situating ocular involvement as a recognised complication of the systemic disease rather than an incidental association (PMID 32160869); recorded as documented association only, with the reverse direction stated and with the evidence density for this particular pair registered as lower than for the rheumatoid-arthritis pair rather than smoothed over.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of systemic lupus erythematosus is established for any individual, and as with the rheumatoid-arthritis edge the located sequence runs from the systemic disease to the eye, so this edge is the reciprocal view and not a claim that scleritis produces lupus. The evidence density for this pair is materially weaker than for the rheumatoid pair and that is stated rather than hidden: unlike the rheumatoid-arthritis edge, no located anchor in this edge reports a systemic-lupus-erythematosus-specific or scleritis-specific effect estimate in its located abstract, and none supplies a scleritis-free comparison group for the ocular outcome, so the edge rests on the population anchor's overall immune-mediated-inflammatory-disease association structure plus the existence of a dedicated ophthalmic-risk analysis in a lupus cohort rather than on a quantified pair-specific estimate. The located cohort analyses are also largely administrative, which limits clinical phenotyping of the scleritis subtype. Individual claims require a dated systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosis meeting contemporary classification criteria with relevant autoantibody profile and complement levels, organ involvement assessment, and a separately dated scleritis diagnosis, and the reviewing clinician should note that the temporal sequence runs from the systemic disease to the ocular manifestation.

### `scotoma` → `cerebrovascular-accident-stroke-residuals` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Occipital infarction is the commonest documented cause of a homonymous visual field defect, and the located evidence both establishes that ranking and characterises the residual defect: a cohort of 36 patients with acute occipital stroke reports that stroke is the most common cause of homonymous visual field defects, that 26 of 36 patients (72 percent) had a visual field defect at onset identified by confrontation or perimetry, and that at follow-up more than one year later 13 patients (36 percent) had a remaining defect comprising 5 homonymous hemianopias, 5 homonymous quadrantanopias, and 3 homonymous scotomas, with macular ganglion cell and inner plexiform layer and retinal nerve fibre layer thickness significantly reduced in each eye in patients with a defect compared to those without (p<0.01 for all comparisons) (PMID 34487632); a case series of three patients with bilateral homonymous visual field defects from bilateral ischaemic strokes reports a right horizontal wedge-shaped homonymous scotoma on perimetry in a patient with a chronic left occipital stroke and acute right thalamic ischaemia, and notes that two of the three patients suffered sequential bilateral strokes and were unaware of the initial scotoma (PMID 30339636); and a lesion-to-field correlation study reports the relationship between peripheral homonymous hemianopia and lesion location using cytoarchitectonic mapping (PMID 21623227); recorded as an ETIOLOGIC association, with the direction of causation stated explicitly and opposite to the edge name.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** The direction of causation is the reverse of the edge name and this is stated in the causation status rather than argued around: the located evidence establishes that the stroke PRODUCES the visual field defect, so this edge records that posterior-circulation infarction is a documented cause of a homonymous scotoma, not that a scotoma produces a stroke. No causation is established in the direction the edge name suggests, and the edge may not be presented that way. Beyond direction, the located designs do not establish that any individual scotoma is stroke-related: the primary cohort requires acute occipital stroke as an entry criterion, so it contains no stroke-free comparison group and cannot estimate the probability that a given scotoma is vascular; the case series is three patients selected precisely for the rarity of their bilateral presentation and is not a frequency estimate; and the lesion-correlation study addresses where lesions map to field defects rather than how often defects occur. A clinically important additional limit is the located report that two of three patients in the case series were unaware of the initial scotoma, so a defect may be clinically silent and its presence in a record cannot be assumed. Individual claims require a dated posterior-circulation or occipital infarction with neuroimaging, a dated perimetry or formal visual field result, and documented visual field testing rather than subjective report.

### `scotoma` → `migraine-headaches` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Scotomatous visual symptoms are among the commonest reported visual aura phenomena in migraine, and the located evidence is unusually explicit about the differential this creates: a systematic review of prospective and retrospective systematic recordings of visual aura symptoms, drawing on 11 retrospective and 3 prospective studies and finding that the number of distinct visual phenomena reported per study ranged from 2 to 23, identifies the most common as flashes of bright light, foggy vision, zigzag lines, SCOTOMA, small bright dots, and heat-wave or water distortion, and states that migraine aura is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and is often clinically difficult to distinguish from other serious neurological disorders such as transient ischaemic attacks and epilepsy (PMID 31146673); a tertiary-care analysis of 165 patients classifies aura by ICHD-III and profiles visual aura type, duration, laterality, and its relation to migraine (PMID 33927518); and a systematic review addresses the differentiation of visual symptoms between retinal migraine and migraine with aura, that is between the two migraine presentations in which a scotomatous defect may appear (PMID 40873917); recorded as an ETIOLOGIC association, with the direction of causation stated explicitly and opposite to the edge name.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** The direction of causation is the reverse of the edge name and is stated in the causation status rather than argued around: the located evidence establishes that migraine PRODUCES the transient scotomatous visual symptom, so this edge records migraine as a documented cause of a transient scotoma and not that a scotoma produces migraine. Beyond direction, the located evidence is weaker than the edge's own differential warning implies: the systematic review pooled no frequencies and reports only the ranked order of reported phenomena, so scotoma is documented as commonly REPORTED without a rate, and the number of distinct phenomena varied from 2 to 23 across the included studies, which means the reported ranking depends heavily on how each study elicited and coded symptoms; the 165-patient analysis is a single tertiary centre in one country with an observational questionnaire design, which is not a population prevalence estimate; and the retinal-versus-with-aura differentiation review addresses a distinction between two migraine subtypes rather than establishing migraine as the cause of any given scotoma. The edge's most important limitation is the one the primary anchor itself raises, namely that a transient scotomatous defect is difficult to distinguish from transient ischaemic attack and from epilepsy, so an individual attribution requires the time course and associated symptoms rather than the visual phenomenon alone.

### `scotoma` → `seizure-disorder` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Occipital lobe epilepsy produces simple visual phenomena and persistent visual field defects at substantial rates, and the located cohort quantifies both while documenting how often the diagnosis is missed: a longitudinal study of 24 adult occipital lobe epilepsy patients identified over 12 months from 1548 patients in a neurologist's service and followed over 12 years reports that occipital lobe epilepsies comprise 5 to 10 percent of focal epilepsies, that 92 percent of these patients had simple visual hallucinations, that these were MISDIAGNOSED IN 40 PERCENT OF CASES, that 75 percent had co-morbid interictal migraine, that 38 percent had VISUAL FIELD DEFECTS, that only 33 percent achieved long-term remission, and that only 2 of 10 patients with a structural aetiology were seizure-free (PMID 33900448); a study of visual search disorders in patients with acute homonymous visual field defects addresses the perceptual consequences of a defect of documented vascular origin, which is the comparator class for the field component of an epileptic presentation (PMID 19500605); and the lesion-to-field cytoarchitectonic study supplies the post-geniculate anatomy that a focal occipital seizure discharges within (PMID 21623227); recorded as an ETIOLOGIC association, with the direction of causation stated explicitly and opposite to the edge name.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** The direction of causation is the reverse of the edge name and is stated in the causation status rather than argued around: the located evidence establishes that focal occipital seizure activity PRODUCES the visual phenomenon and the field defect, so this edge records occipital lobe epilepsy as a documented cause of a scotomatous or field defect and not that a scotoma produces epilepsy. The located evidence is additionally self-limiting in an important way that is registered rather than glossed: the cohort reports that the simple visual hallucinations were misdiagnosed in 40 percent of cases, which means that in a substantial fraction of real presentations the epileptic origin is not recognised, so a documented visual-field defect attributed elsewhere may in fact be epileptic, and conversely a recorded defect without a seizure diagnosis may understate the epileptic cause. The cohort is small at 24 patients drawn from a single neurologist's service, so it is enriched for complex or diagnostically uncertain cases and does not estimate community prevalence, and it reports adult disease only. **Proposition (associationBasis):** Multiple sclerosis produces visual field defects through both pre- and post-geniculate mechanisms, and the located evidence documents each: a review of visual impairment in multiple sclerosis states that visual impairment is one of the most common and disabling manifestations of the disease, that visual dysfunction related to optic neuritis and brainstem involvement is well recognised, that visual impairment associated with POST-GENICULATE visual pathways including the optic radiations and visual cortex remains comparatively under-studied and under-recognised in clinical practice, and that increasing evidence from advanced neuroimaging, optical coherence tomography, and neuropsychological testing demonstrates that lesions affecting post-geniculate white and grey matter contribute to both symptomatic and subclinical visual dysfunction, with the abnormalities listed as HOMONYMOUS VISUAL FIELD DEFECTS, visuoperceptual dysfunction, visual cognitive impairment, and higher-order ocular motor abnormalities (PMID 42729962); a retrospective population-based single-centre study of 192 patients with multiple sclerosis reports that ocular symptoms were reported by 120 patients, determines the proportion with afferent and efferent visual disturbances, assesses visual evoked potentials in detecting visual pathway abnormality, and identifies ocular findings that represented the initial clinical manifestation of the disease (PMID 41798516); and a StatPearls chapter on optic neuritis supplies the pre-geniculate route by which the demyelinating lesion produces a field defect (PMID 32496733); recorded as an ETIOLOGIC association, with the direction of causation stated explicitly and opposite to the edge name.

The evidence quality is additionally uneven between the two anatomical routes and that is registered rather than smoothed: the post-geniculate route is described by its own anchor as comparatively UNDER-STUDIED and UNDER-RECOGNISED in clinical practice, so the best-characterised route, optic neuritis, is represented here by a tertiary StatPearls chapter rather than by a primary cohort, and that asymmetry is disclosed. The primary cohort is single-centre and retrospective, uses structured questionnaires completed at routine visits, and reports ocular symptoms in 120 of 192 patients without a comparator population, so it establishes that ocular involvement is common in multiple sclerosis rather than estimating how often a given scotoma is demyelinating. ### `seborrheic-dermatitis` → `parkinsons-disease` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Seborrhoeic dermatitis is the most frequently reported skin finding in Parkinson's disease and the association is bidirectional in the located evidence, with a severity gradient running in both directions: a scoping review of systemic comorbidities associated with seborrhoeic dermatitis reports that nearly half of Parkinson's disease patients in one study also had seborrhoeic dermatitis, that as the severity of Parkinson's disease symptoms increases the development of seborrhoeic dermatitis is observed to occur at a much higher rate, and that the burden of seborrhoeic dermatitis is positively correlated to the severity of Parkinson's symptoms, and it explicitly frames the whole comorbidity literature as highlighting the complex nature of seborrhoeic dermatitis and underscoring the necessity of further research (PMID 39669846); a cross-sectional study examining the association of seborrhoeic dermatitis and Parkinson's disease is registered as the dedicated paired-design source for this edge (PMID 39313034); and a narrative review sets out the genetic, lipid, fungal-microbiome, and neuroinflammatory links proposed between the two diseases, which is the located source for the candidate mechanisms rather than for the association itself (PMID 42650087); recorded as documented association only, with the direction recorded as unresolved and with the scoping review's own nulls for the most commonly cited seborrhoeic comorbidities carried openly on the file.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence supports association in both directions without resolving which is antecedent: the scoping review frames the finding from the Parkinson's population, reporting how many Parkinson's patients also have seborrhoeic dermatitis and how that prevalence rises with Parkinson's severity, while the file's own identity is the skin disease, so the clinically operative arrow runs Parkinson's to seborrhoeic dermatitis and this edge is the reciprocal view. Whether the association reflects a shared upstream driver, in which alpha-synuclein biology, altered sebum lipid composition, and Malassezia proliferation each plausibly contribute to both, or a genuine consequence of Parkinson motor dysfunction on facial sebaceous function, cannot be separated by the located cross-sectional design, and the review's own proposal of genetic, lipid, fungal-microbiome, and neuroinflammatory links is explicitly a set of hypotheses rather than tested mechanisms. The scoping review also records that in one cross-sectional study of patients with seborrhoeic dermatitis the most common systemic comorbidities were hypertension and diabetes, that this finding was NOT statistically significant, and that obesity was common but ALSO not significant, which is registered as a null here because those are the comorbidities a reviewer is most likely to assume. Individual claims require a dated Parkinson's diagnosis with motor and non-motor staging, a dated seborrhoeic dermatitis diagnosis with distribution documented, and a dated assessment of whether the skin disease predated, postdated, or tracked the neurological staging.

### `seborrheic-dermatitis` → `hiv-aids` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Seborrhoeic dermatitis is among the commonest dermatological diagnoses in people living with HIV, and the located evidence supplies both a pooled prevalence and a histopathological signature: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 145 articles involving 41,285 people with HIV identified approximately 28,448 patients with dermatological disease, and among 60,064 dermatological events found the most prevalent conditions to be oral candidiasis at 8.88 percent, dermatophytosis, SEBORRHEIC DERMATITIS, warts, and herpes zoster, with an overall prevalence of dermatological disease of 76 percent (95 percent CI 72 to 81) and significant heterogeneity at I squared 97 percent (PMID 41162862); a prospective clinicopathological study of 30 HIV-seropositive adults presenting with seborrhoeic-like dermatitis found 50 percent showed severe or very severe disease and 6 patients (20.0 percent) presented with erythroderma, and confirmed that confluent parakeratosis, necrotic keratinocytes, plasma cells, neutrophils with leukocytoclasia, and leukoexocytosis are histopathological clues to seborrhoeic-like dermatitis occurring in HIV-seropositive patients, so that the presence of these features in a skin biopsy is itself a clue to the diagnosis of HIV (PMID 32379092); and the scoping review of seborrhoeic comorbidities reports that HIV is a disease with higher incidence of seborrhoeic dermatitis, while noting that the prevalence of comorbid seborrhoeic dermatitis MAY BE DECREASING as antiretroviral therapy use increases (PMID 39669846); recorded as documented association only, with the primary anchor's heterogeneity and the located explicit null on severity correlation carried openly.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence is genuinely mixed in a way this edge records rather than smooths over: the meta-analysis reports a 76 percent overall prevalence of ANY dermatological disease with I squared 97 percent, so its seborrhoeic-dermatitis contribution is one component of a very heterogeneous literature and must not be read as an individual risk figure; the clinicopathological study explicitly found NO significant correlation between seborrhoeic-like dermatitis severity and CD4 count, viral load, or antiretroviral therapy, which is a direct null on the natural assumption that the skin disease tracks HIV disease activity, and that null is registered on the face of this edge; the scoping review notes the prevalence of comorbid seborrhoeic dermatitis may be DECREASING as antiretroviral therapy increases, which cuts against any assumption of a stable or rising contemporary association; and the histopathological study is 30 patients from a single South African dermatology clinic, so the histological clues are suggestive rather than diagnostic. Individual claims require a dated HIV diagnosis with CD4 count, viral load, and antiretroviral therapy history, a dated seborrhoeic or seborrhoeic-like dermatitis diagnosis with severity documented, and where the biopsy signature is relied upon, dermatopathology review.

### `seborrheic-keratosis` → `colorectal-cancer` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** An abrupt eruptive onset of multiple seborrhoeic keratoses is the Leser-Trelat sign, a cutaneous paraneoplastic phenomenon whose most frequently reported underlying malignancies are gastrointestinal, and the located evidence frames it explicitly as an early-detection signal for colon cancer: a case report and review describes the Leser-Trelat syndrome as an UNDERDIAGNOSED cutaneous paraneoplastic syndrome that could aid in EARLY DETECTION OF COLON CANCER, and sets out the differential diagnoses, the completed workup, and current treatment options for a patient presenting with this pattern (PMID 37814771); a second case report documents the Leser-Trelat sign as an initial manifestation of synchronous prostate and bladder cancer, establishing the phenomenon as non-specific across tumour types rather than colon-specific (PMID 41158917); and a third case report documents the sign in a patient with gastric adenocarcinoma, supporting the gastrointestinal signal (PMID 37843094); recorded as a screening-signal association only, with the mechanism mismatch between the registered vocabulary and the paraneoplastic phenomenon disclosed on the face of the edge rather than resolved by inventing a category.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of colorectal cancer is established for any individual, and this edge asserts something materially weaker than a causal route: the located evidence supports the Leser-Trelat sign as a MARKER that may precede detection of an underlying internal malignancy, not a mechanism by which a keratosis produces cancer. The direction of the clinical arrow runs from the internal malignancy to the skin eruption, so the edge records the skin presentation as a possible screening signal and NOT as a cause of the tumour, and the reviewing clinician must understand that an individual claim on this basis would be a claim that the keratosis warrants a malignancy workup rather than a claim that the keratosis caused the cancer. The association is also substantially non-specific, as the located prostate and bladder case report shows, and the located evidence assembled for this edge is dominated by case reports and a descriptive clinical review rather than by a cohort, a systematic review, or a pooled estimate, so no frequency, no positive predictive value, and no incidence of malignancy in patients with eruptive keratoses can be quoted from these references. Individual claims require the documented eruptive onset with dated photographs or description, a malignancy workup with the results recorded, and an established cancer diagnosis independent of the skin finding.

### `selective-mutism` → `social-anxiety-disorder` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Social phobia is near-universal in selective mutism and is the single best-established associated condition, with two independent designs reporting very high rates: a random-effects meta-analysis of 22 eligible studies (N=837) pooled the prevalence of comorbid anxiety disorders in selective mutism and found that 80 percent of children with selective mutism carried an additional anxiety disorder, NOTABLY SOCIAL PHOBIA AT 69 PERCENT, while reporting considerable heterogeneity that remained unexplained by a priori specified moderators and concluding that the disorders are NOT DISCRETE, SEPARABLE CATEGORIES (PMID 31650460); and a comparative behavioral study of 95 children and adolescents with selective mutism against 74 with social phobia, 46 with other internalizing disorders, and 119 typically developing controls, using the Child Behavior Checklist with diagnostic-interview comorbidity assessment, found social phobia detected in 94 PERCENT of children with selective mutism while showing that the two groups differ, with selective mutism more frequently carrying lifetime separation anxiety disorder (45 versus 26 percent) and oppositional defiant disorder (22 versus 5 percent) and LESS frequently carrying generalized anxiety disorder (6 versus 20 percent) and major depression (12 versus 26 percent) (PMID 27089281); a parent-reported clinical characterization of 230 children with diagnosed or suspected selective mutism reports that anxiety AND SOCIAL ANXIETY SYMPTOMS WERE ELEVATED, with age of onset and diagnosis both earlier than previously reported and an average diagnostic delay of 2 years (PMID 37650960); recorded as documented association only, with the near-ubiquity of the co-diagnosis explicitly framed as challenging the separability of the two diagnoses rather than as establishing a route between them.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence is better read as a challenge to the diagnostic boundary than as a causal claim: the meta-analysis states explicitly that the finding that selective mutism is often diagnosed in combination with anxiety disorders indicates that these disorders are NOT DISCRETE, SEPARABLE CATEGORIES, and that this finding DOES NOT ELUDICATE the relation between selective mutism and anxiety as an aetiological mechanism OR AS A SYMPTOMATIC FEATURE, so the co-occurrence cannot be used to argue that one produces the other. The meta-analysis also carries considerable heterogeneity that remained unexplained, so its 69 percent social-phobia figure is a pooled estimate with real between-study spread, and its own stated recommendation is that research strategies for assessing anxiety be broadened before the relationship is classified. The comparative study establishes a diagnostic overlap, not an aetiology. Individual claims require a dated social anxiety disorder diagnosis with documented fear of social evaluation, a dated selective mutism diagnosis documenting speech absence in specific social contexts with normal speech in others, and a clinical determination of which diagnosis is primary, because at a 94 percent co-detection rate the two diagnoses are frequently recorded as alternatives for the same presentation rather than as separate conditions in one patient.

- Is the citation metadata exact against the PubMed record?

### `selective-mutism` → `separation-anxiety-disorder` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Separation anxiety is markedly over-represented in selective mutism relative to its comparison group, which is the located evidence that distinguishes the two anxiety phenotypes rather than collapsing them: the comparative behavioral study of 95 children and adolescents with selective mutism against 74 with social phobia found that selective-mutism participants were MORE FREQUENTLY AFFECTED BY LIFETIME SEPARATION ANXIETY DISORDER, 45 PERCENT AGAINST 26 PERCENT, while simultaneously being less affected by generalized anxiety disorder and major depression, so the two conditions present different comorbidity profiles (PMID 27089281); the same profile is what makes selective mutism separable from social phobia rather than a variant of it, since the two diagnoses load on different additional conditions (PMID 27089281); a family-accommodation study of 38 children with selective mutism, 28 with selective mutism plus comorbid anxiety disorders, 34 with other anxiety disorders, and 30 with non-anxiety disorders found that accommodation in the selective-mutism sample was prevalent though reported at lower frequency and with lower parental distress than expected, with NO CORRELATION between accommodation and selective-mutism symptom severity (PMID 40586947); and the 230-child parent-reported characterization reporting elevated anxiety and social anxiety symptoms supplies the contemporary presentation context (PMID 37650960); recorded as documented association only, with the reverse-and-parallel nature of the relationship disclosed.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the direction of the relationship is genuinely unresolved: both conditions are childhood anxiety diagnoses recorded concurrently, the located comparative study reports LIFETIME separation anxiety disorder in 45 percent of children with selective mutism but does not establish whether the separation anxiety preceded the mutism, followed it, or was diagnosed alongside it, and a lifetime prevalence figure is by construction uninformative about sequence. A substantial diagnostic component is likely, since a child who cannot speak to a parent on school morning is difficult to distinguish from a child with separation distress, and the located family-accommodation anchor makes the reverse direction concrete: parental accommodation is described as a maintaining factor in the selective-mutism picture, which is a parent-to-child process that could equally intensify separation distress. The family-accommodation study also reports NO CORRELATION between accommodation and symptom severity, which is a direct null against the assumption that accommodation severity tracks illness severity. Individual claims require dated, separately signed diagnoses of both conditions with the chronology established, and clinician determination of whether the two diagnoses describe one presentation or two conditions.

### `separation-anxiety-disorder` → `anxiety-disorder` — ASSOCIATION_ONLY

**Proposition (associationBasis):** Separation anxiety disorder sits inside the anxiety-disorder family and the located population evidence places it among the diagnoses driving the documented rise in childhood anxiety, with a comorbidity burden that makes an additional anxiety diagnosis the most probable documented accompaniment: a repeated cross-sectional analysis of nationally representative probability samples of 13,561 children and young people aged 5 to 16 in England across the 2004 and 2017 Mental Health of Children and Young People survey waves, classified by ICD-10 using the Development and Well-Being Assessment, found the prevalence of emotional disorders rose from 3.9 to 6.0 percent (relative ratio 1.63, 95 percent CI 1.38 to 1.91), largely driven by anxiety disorders rising from 3.5 to 5.4 percent (relative ratio 1.63, 95 percent CI 1.37 to 1.93), with the LARGEST relative changes for PANIC DISORDER, SEPARATION ANXIETY, SOCIAL PHOBIA AND POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER, and with comorbid psychiatric conditions present in OVER A THIRD of children with emotional disorders, the most common being conduct disorder (PMID 40546093); a study of separation anxiety disorder in youth with mitral valve prolapse documents the condition with associated parental attitudes and anxiety-sensitivity findings, establishing it as a clinically studied and separately diagnosed entity rather than a descriptive label (PMID 42228469); and a clinical reference chapter on the disorder supplies the diagnostic framing (PMID 32809628); recorded as documented association only, with the population trend evidence and the individual-level comorbidity evidence held explicitly apart.

**Causation boundary (causationStatus):** Neither causation nor aggravation of a generalised anxiety disorder is established for any individual, and the located evidence is weaker for this specific pairing than its volume suggests: the England survey reports AGGREGATE prevalence and TREND for the anxiety-disorder class and names separation anxiety among the four diagnoses with the largest relative increases, but it does NOT report a separation-anxiety-to-anxiety-disorder comorbidity rate, so the 13,561 children establish the scale of the anxiety-disorder burden in the population rather than the probability that a child with separation anxiety also carries a generalised anxiety disorder. The over-a-third comorbidity figure is reported across children with emotional disorders as a class, which includes both anxiety and depressive disorders, and the most common comorbid condition is conduct disorder, which is not the target of this edge. No located anchor in this edge supplies a separation-anxiety-specific comorbidity rate, a longitudinal design, or a non-anxiety comparison group. Individual claims require a dated separation anxiety disorder diagnosis meeting criteria, a dated and separately documented generalised anxiety disorder diagnosis, and clinician determination of whether the diagnoses are co-occurring conditions or a re-specification of one presentation, since the two overlap in childhood and are frequently re-classified as a child develops.
